layout.label: The Problem
layout.heading: Advisors are stuck in AI's messy middle.

children.text: Most advisors we talk to are already using AI in some form. They pull up their favorite AI before a client meeting to synthesize a document, draft an agenda, or make sense of a fact pattern they haven't had time to fully digest.

It works well enough. But it wasn't built for client work, and the gaps show up fast: no boundaries between engagements, no audit trail, no way to carry context forward from the last conversation or between members of the advisory team.

At the same time, business owners are arriving with more information than ever. They've asked AI what their business is worth, what questions to bring to their advisor, whether they need one at all. The information asymmetry that once defined the advisory relationship is compressing.

layout.closer: The work is changing, but until now, the tools haven't.

children.text: The advisors who see this shift recognize that when the client shows up more informed, the conversation starts at a higher level, and the trust, judgement, and accountability they bring to the table becomes
even more valuable
AI's messy middle is about building a practice that delivers on this new reality.
Most advisors are running so hard to keep up with each engagement that they haven't had the bandwidth to step back and think about their practice as a system.

hero.headline: We're building for advisors who believe practice is more than process.
hero.subheadline: ELLA was built from conversations, not assumptions. Over a year of listening before a line of code was written.

children.text: Small businesses are more than engines of the economy. They represent the life’s work of their owners, anchors in their communities, and legacies passed through families. When it’s time to move on, they deserve more than a transaction. They deserve a future; one that carries forward what they built.

We believe exits should honor both the business and the owner: the risks taken, the relationships forged, and the impact made. But too often, owners are pushed toward quick deals, private equity offers that won’t protect the legacy, or liquidation.
We believe trusted advisors are the key to changing this status quo. When owners have someone who sees beyond numbers — seeing the story and legacy of the business — better exits are possible.
We’re building ELLA to make that easier.

layout.heading: We started with conversations, not code.

children.text: Before we built anything, we spent a year in conversation with the advisors who would use it. CEPAs running solo practices. CPAs doing exit work alongside their tax practice. Wealth managers thinking ten years ahead. M&A brokers who’ve been through hundreds of deals.
We asked the same question every time: where do you get stuck?
The answer shifted. Twice.
First, we learned advisors didn’t need another monolithic platform. They needed a system that could hold context across their entire practice while letting them work the way they already work.

Second, we learned “exit planning” was the starting point, not the ceiling. The advisors we kept meeting were guiding business owners through consequential decisions across every stage of building a significant business. The common thread was trust as the foundation.
We built ELLA around both of those lessons.

layout.heading: Structured discovery built around your priorities.

children.text: What makes you unique? We think part of it is your methodology: the questions you ask, the order you ask them, the way you read between the lines of a balance sheet and a conversation. We built fact finding so it holds that structure without flattening it into someone else's process.

Start with research-calibrated templates across M&A readiness, succession planning, personal readiness, and vertical-specific domains. Or build your own from scratch. Group business factors by the categories that match how you think, add questions, reorder them, and layer in notes that link directly to each discovery item. As documents come in, the system cross-references uploaded files against your open questions and surfaces suggested answers for your review.
Every answer, every note, and every document becomes context that carries forward into Sensemaking and Deliverables. Nothing gets lost between intake and analysis.

children.text: When you open a sensemaking session, the system already knows your client. It assembles context from everything in the workspace: fact finding answers, uploaded documents, prior conversations, and the specific business factors you scope in. We call this prompt composition. Rather than dumping everything into a single context window, the system selects, structures, and layers relevant data alongside domain-specific analytical skills: financial hygiene, owner readiness, risk breakdown, document analysis, valuation prep. These are structured frameworks calibrated to how advisors evaluate a business, not generic prompts dressed up with a label.

This is what separates purpose-built sensemaking from dropping files into a Claude project or a ChatGPT thread. A general-purpose AI doesn't know what a normalized EBITDA add-back is, doesn't understand why owner dependency is a value driver, and can't tell a succession plan that's been operationalized from one that exists only on paper. We built that domain intelligence into the system so you don't have to prompt-engineer your way to useful output every time you sit down.

galleryItems.caption: Context-Aware Analysis
galleryItems.subcaption: Every session draws from the full workspace. Select specific business factor groups or analyze everything at once. The system knows what you've collected and structures it before the model ever sees it.

galleryItems.caption: Domain-Specific Analytical Skills
galleryItems.subcaption: Financial hygiene, owner readiness, risk breakdown, document analysis, and valuation prep. These run based on what you ask, calibrated to how advisors evaluate a business.

galleryItems.caption: Memory

layout.heading: Adding context with every input
layout.promptText: What are the biggest risks to this exit timeline?
layout.footerLeft: One question. Five ingredients. Six months of structured engagement data.

items.heading: Owner dependency is the primary risk factor.
items.body: Turner holds all key client relationships and sole vendor signatory authority. No documented succession for operations.
items.annotationDetail: Management team assessment and key-person dependency, answered during discovery.

items.heading: Revenue concentration creates buyer risk.
items.body: Three clients at 62% of trailing revenue. Stress-scenario EBITDA impact: -$160K.
items.annotationDetail: Three years of financial statements, analyzed via Financial Hygiene.

items.heading: Exit timeline is constrained by buyer pool.
items.body: 18-month target assumes broad buyer access, but no-earn-out preference narrows viable acquirers.
items.annotationDetail: Advisor correction: owner prefers no earn-out structures.

items.heading: Wealth gap is manageable but timeline-sensitive.
items.body: $1.2M desired vs. $160K gap at current FMV. Achievable in 24 months; compressed timeline raises execution risk.
items.annotationDetail: Owner Readiness calculated the wealth gap. Risk Breakdown linked it to timeline.

items.heading: Buy-sell agreement requires immediate attention.
items.body: Life-insurance funded, unreviewed for three years. Valuation methodology clause outdated.
items.annotationDetail: Valuation prep flagged the outdated buy-sell clause two weeks prior.

layout.heading: Built to make sense of the work that happens beyond the desk

children.text: The last thing an advisor needs is another tool that produces generic 90-page reports nobody reads. Deliverables live inside the same workspace as your fact finding and sensemaking, so every document is grounded in real data from the engagement, not copy-pasted from a chat window.

Pull insights directly from a sensemaking conversation into a document. Use the block-based editor to compose, rearrange, and refine, and invite collaborators to review and comment in real time. AI assists with drafting, but the advisor controls the final word, because these documents carry your name and your reputation.

galleryItems.caption: Block-Based Editor
galleryItems.subcaption: Type / to insert blocks for formatting or referencing client data. Press space to draft with Sensemaking inline. It works like a doc you already know, connected to the data you've already collected.

galleryItems.caption: Templates
galleryItems.subcaption: Start from deliverable templates that match your practice: exit readiness scorecards, preliminary financial audits, value acceleration plans. Customize the structure and reuse across engagements.

galleryItems.caption: Multiplayer & Comments
galleryItems.subcaption: Invite collaborators to review deliverables and leave comments directly in the document. Threaded conversations keep feedback organized and connected to the specific content it references.

galleryItems.caption: Connected to Context
galleryItems.subcaption: Turn a sensemaking response into a deliverable with one action. Embed upload fields that connect directly to fact finding, so clients can contribute data from inside the document itself. The data flows both ways.

children.text: The CPA running tax analysis, the attorney reviewing the buy-sell agreement, the wealth manager stress-testing retirement projections, and the business owner contributing context only they can provide. They all need to see the right information, contribute in the right places, and trust that their data stays where it belongs.

We built the collaborator interface as a purpose-built experience for everyone on the exit team who isn't the lead advisor. Collaborators see only what's been shared with them: the fact finding questions assigned to them, the published deliverables relevant to their role, and the documents that require their input. No sidebar clutter. No billing screens. No features they don't need.

For business owners, this is where they contribute financial data during fact finding, review deliverables as the engagement progresses, and comment on documents that directly affect their business. How they experience the platform reflects directly on the advisor who invited them.

galleryItems.caption: Role-Scoped Access
galleryItems.subcaption: Collaborators see only what's shared with them. Fact finding questions, published deliverables, and relevant documents, scoped by workspace role. No access to advisor-only features like sensemaking or billing.

galleryItems.caption: Direct Data Contribution
galleryItems.subcaption: Business owners and team members answer fact finding questions directly in the platform. Their answers flow into the same structured data the advisor uses for sensemaking and deliverables.

galleryItems.caption: Deliverable Review & Comments
galleryItems.subcaption: Collaborators review published deliverables and leave comments directly in the document. Threaded conversations keep feedback organized and connected to the content it references.
